THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri.Shripad V. Shastri, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri.F.S.Dabali, learned counsel for the respondent.
2.

The claimant seeking for enhancement of compensation preferred this appeal challenging the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru in MVC.No.3009/2019 dated 05.12.2020.
As against the claim for Rs.15,00,000/- in total, the Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.1,95,600/- as compensation and aggrieved by the same, the claimant is before this Court.
3. It is an undisputed fact that due to the road traffic accident, the appellant sustained fracture of right femur.
Also, the fact that appellant underwent a surgery i.e., closed reduction and internal fixation with IMIL nailing is not in dispute.

Arguing the matter, Sri.Shripad V. NC:
2024:KHC:32434 Shastri, learned counsel for the appellant contends that the appellant took extensive treatment by spending lakhs of rupees but he could not attain normalcy.
Learned counsel states that appellant is disabled and the percentage of disability is established by examining the Doctor who assessed the disability.
However, without considering the evidence produced, the Tribunal awarded a meager sum as compensation under all the heads and therefore, the amount awarded as compensation is required to be enhanced.

4. On the other hand, Sri.F.S.Dabali, learned counsel for the respondent contends that the appellant did not lose his earning power by the injuries sustained and he continued his occupation even after the accident.
Learned counsel states that the appellant who examined himself as PW.1, during the course of cross-examination stated that he received part of salary during treatment period.

Learned counsel also states that the medical expenditure incurred is reimbursed by the Star Health Insurance Company and thus, the appellant did not spend any NC: 2024:KHC:32434 amount from his pocket towards treatment.

Learned counsel also states that the Tribunal awarded sufficient amount under all heads and thus, there is no need for any interference.
5. The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.1,95,600/- as compensation divided under the following heads:

sentences.text:
The Tribunal deducting the amount that is paid by the Star Health Insurance Company Limited,
held that the medical expenses incurred by the appellant is Rs.5,600/-.
The Tribunal awarded the said amount under the head "treatment, hospitalization, medicines and transportation".

However,
the said amount does not include transportation expenses.
Also it is not the case of the appellant or indeed the case of the respondent that the appellant received entire salary during laid up period.

Having considered the nature of the injuries and the surgery underwent, this Court is of the view that the appellant would not have attended his work as a normal person atleast for a period of four months.
However, the Tribunal has not awarded any amount towards 'loss of earning' during laid up period.
7. Sri.Shripad V. Shastri, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is required to undergo another surgery for removal of implants.
PW.3-Dr.Nagaraj B.N. has clearly stated that the appellant needs another NC: 2024:KHC:32434 surgery for removal of implants.
Also the amount awarded under the head 'extra nourishment, food, diet and attendant charges' is grossly inadequate.

Therefore, this Court is of the view that a global sum of Rs.1,00,000/- is required to be awarded in addition to the amount that is awarded by the Tribunal in view of the fact that the Tribunal failed to award any amount for the transportation expenses incurred, towards the 'loss earning during laid up period and that the amount awarded towards 'future medical expenses' and 'extra nourishment,
food, diet and attendant charges' is grossly inadequate.

Thus, the appeal is disposed of with the following:

3 ORDER i) The appeal is allowed-in-part.
